seen.cipher: Syllabic or nomenclator signs with word spaces and points (curved and barred letter-like signs, e.g. a ꝓ-like and ∂-like family) filling c.44r from top to bottom, and three lines on c.46v after 'Al capitan Tapia en Massa, la qual ...'. The slip on c.43r is clear Spanish, not cipher: a list of heads ('del sacar de la gente', 'de los 4000 ducados del donativo', 'de los de Rauena', 'Mendoca en Orbitello y Porto Ercole', 'Tapia en Massa') that reads as an agenda or summary and gives no signs. On c.46v a clear marginal note of about six lines ('por fas o nefas se tenga ... el tiempo se resolvera ... el Trivulcio ... el Rey y a los hijos') stands beside the 3 cipher lines; I could not tell whether it paraphrases them or is part of the letter, and it is not an interlinear decipherment. No decipherment is written between the lines of c.44r, which is the main cipher, and no clear copy of it is bound with it. Note: the closing says Siena, not Rome (Mendoza was governor of Siena).

seen.extent: One page (one image): two columns of the calendar text (feast of St Symeon Stylites), with one line of about 30 signs along the bottom margin, plus a second short line of about 20 letters in heavier ink at the foot of the right column.
seen.cipher: The bottom-margin line is written in Greek letters (with a few accent-like marks) that make no Greek words in sequence, e.g. a run beginning 'ὑ ο ς β α λ ...' too small to read reliably; the short line at the foot of the right column ('ὦ κ α ι ρ φ ε κ ...' as far as legible) is also not Greek text. This matches the NYPL description 'a prayer by the scribe in bottom margin written in a cryptographic system' (a substitution scribal cryptogram). No decipherment, plaintext gloss or key is written on the page, and the record gives none. At this resolution the letters cannot be transcribed with certainty, so a transcription needs a better image.
